question: Should OpenClaw accept this externally verified approval seam once resolver identity is host-derived and the compatibility, denial, persistence, audit, and default-decision rules are fully specified?
rationale: The proposal grants plugins authority to complete approval-gated tool execution, so the permanent API and trust boundary require explicit owner acceptance even if the RFC text and reference implementation are technically sound.

options.title: Refine the narrow seam
options.body: Keep the RFC open and require the host-derived identity, deny-dominant composition, version gating, existing approval semantics, audit timing, safe default, and runtime proof before acceptance.

options.title: Reject plugin resolution authority
options.body: Keep final approval resolution exclusively in core and require external verifiers to return evidence through a less-authoritative host callback.

options.title: Broaden the plugin contract
options.body: Design a general plugin-defined approval-action API, accepting the larger compatibility and security surface instead of this narrow verifier-specific seam.

recommendation.title: Refine the narrow seam
recommendation.body: Keep the RFC open and require the host-derived identity, deny-dominant composition, version gating, existing approval semantics, audit timing, safe default, and runtime proof before acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the latest concrete acceptance requirements and are the clearest available decision owner in the RFC discussion.
